en.html:
The bandits had made their base on a small mountain outside town.
Geology would attach it to the rugged mountain range in the north. Practically speaking, too big for a hill, too small for a mountain. Small mountain only. Even the land could not secure a proper designation.

Naturally, the town's children used to play here. Warning shots and naked blades had removed them, every last one. The children liked this mountain, but for the bandits it was an even better property.

Enough height to intimidate the town, no difficulty coming or going. If they called it Canaan, their promised land, on what grounds could I object?
The god making such rotten promises, however, I would prefer not to deal with.

So much for the hope. Crushed without any difficulty.

They had led me into the fort, where the bandit chief heard me out. Then she laughed for some time. Then for some more time. After laughing for a further quantity of time, she finished the matter in one word.

All that air, and the answer had needed so little. Somewhere inside the first ho there must already have been a no. But no, let it mature. Let the visitor stand there while rejection acquires the proper atmosphere. I had come to discuss the town's future; a respectable portion of that future had now passed inside this woman's throat.

Not even a corner where an argument could get its foot in.

A smile.

A pitying laugh escaped with her breath, and she took one step. That smoothness, that suppleness: her ability was clear from that much only.

Strong.

As I had known from the beginning.

Stronger than me.

That too I had considered at least an even chance.

Which was why I had treated her with contempt.

If talking failed, settle it through a contest with the chief. A fine plan. Only the small matter of making certain I won had been giving difficulty.

The strength of Rokuhara's army did not need fresh discussion. Especially its warriors, its dragoons: search the whole world and few could match them. That was why GHQ had accepted their surrender and paid for it with the right to govern Yamato.

This woman had served in that same Rokuhara. Served well enough to secure something very close to complete loyalty. Even after losing her military position, she still had her men; about that there could be no doubt.

In the shogunate army, a warrior commanding infantry was often the head or heir of a middle-ranking warrior house, and the soldiers were his own clan and retainers. Their bond of lord and servant had not been made yesterday. Tradition was behind it.

Even then, had the chief been weak and useless, the men could quite naturally have abandoned her as soon as her position went. Tradition may support loyalty; on tradition alone, nothing will stand.

First and foremost, she had the ability to call herself a Rokuhara warrior without shame. That ability was keeping her men here. In fighting prowess, she was probably not accustomed to being left behind.

Fight properly, and my chance of winning was small.
To win, I had to make her careless.

Simply issuing a challenge would not do. An ordinary townsman challenges a warrior: nine parts contempt, yes, but one part caution would remain.

With that one part still there, where would the opening come from?
My chances would remain small.

So I treated her with contempt.
Let her see the complete fool who thinks, only a woman, what is she going to do?

If the performance worked, anger and contempt together would make her want more than victory. She would want to overwhelm me.

Her swordwork would become broad and careless. And the stroke would not be lethal.

Kill me at once, and how would she make me suffer the humiliation? Most likely she would take an arm or a leg.

...If I could bring the situation that far into my hands, then even an opponent more skilled than me—

Tonight Hikaru was resting quietly. Her breathing too sounded somewhat easier. Easier than before, that was all.

Not the smallest sign of recovery. Life's colour kept leaving her; only the speed varied. Today it was leaving slowly. Each day was still bringing Hikaru closer to death. In that, no change at all.

I had returned late, so I had not reported to the main house tonight. Straight home, and the account given only to my foster mother.

She was happy I was safe. The business at the bandit fort, however, had not pleased her. This was not the best possible resolution; that much I could read in her face.

I felt the same. Otherwise I would have called at the main house even at that hour, rudeness or no rudeness.

...I still thought there had been no other move.

In the woman's face, acceptance was plainly missing. Much more than 'I lost,' she had been thinking, 'Again, and I will win.' Of that I had no doubt.

The bandits too were probably not satisfied. Probably even less than she was.

But the contest had been held under a clear agreement.

Only spoken, yes. That was not much of a problem. Everyone had witnessed the promise, and the result had been perfectly clear.

Someone born into a warrior house would hardly pretend such a fact had not occurred. The promise would be kept. It ought to be kept.

I felt the same. Otherwise I would have called at the main house even at that hour, rudeness or no rudeness.

...I still thought there had been no other move.

In the woman's face, acceptance was plainly missing. Much more than 'I lost,' she had been thinking, 'Again, and I will win.' Of that I had no doubt.

The bandits too were probably not satisfied. Probably even less than she was.

But the contest had been held under a clear agreement.

Only spoken, yes. That was not much of a problem. Everyone had witnessed the promise, and the result had been perfectly clear.

Someone born into a warrior house would hardly pretend such a fact had not occurred. The promise would be kept. It ought to be kept.

今夜の光は安静にしている。

と死に近付いている事実は変わらない。

　帰りが遅くなったので、今日のところは本家へ報告
するのを控えた。
　家へ直帰し、養母へ経過を伝えるに留めた。

　養母は俺の無事こそ喜んでくれたものの、山賊砦で
の一部始終についてはあまり良い顔をしなかった。
　最善の形で解決した――とは、考えていないことが
窺えた。

　俺も同様の思いだった。
　そうでなければ、夜分に訪いを入れる非礼を犯して
でも本家に寄っていったろう。

　……あの手しか無かったとは、思うのだが。

　女首領の表情は詳細に観察するまでもなく、納得と
いう成分を欠いていた。
　負けたと思うよりも、もう一度やれば勝つとの思い
の方が遥かに深かったことは疑いない。

　山賊たちとて納得などしていないだろう。
　おそらくは首領以上に。

　しかし、あれは明確な取り決めのもと行われた勝負
である。

　口約束に過ぎないが、それはさして問題ではない。
　約束は環視の中で確かに取り交わされたし、決着も
明々白々だった。

　仮にも武家の出である者が、確かな事実に頬被りを
決め込むとは考えにくい。
　約束は守られるだろう――守られる筈だ。

Whatever else, tomorrow I would report to the main house. That much I decided.

Would they be satisfied? Who knew. It depended on how I explained.

Bandits they might be, but once they had been samurai. Some warrior's pride remained. At least they would not continue openly plundering the town—put it that way, and perhaps I could persuade the main house.

It felt like playing a trick. But with Hikaru's illness giving us no time, what choice was there? And my faith in a warrior's pride, that part was not false.

en.html:
Memory of the beginning.

Mother taking Father.
Father taken by Mother.
Myself losing Father.

Again.
Then again.

The same dream I keep seeing.
In darkness with no end.

For this existence called Hikaru, only that is permitted.

The dark will not release me.
Here itself I must rot; that is its order.

Not to move. That also is its order.

Yes.
From here, Hikaru must not move.

If I, Hikaru, whose Father was taken, set this life in motion,
it would be to bring Father back.

I, who was robbed,
live and move only to take back.

But permission for that is not there.

—Father belongs to Mother. Mother belongs to Father.
A child taking Father from Mother: the human way strictly forbids it.

Hikaru is human.
Against the human way I cannot go.

Follow the human way,
and I am not allowed to take Father back from Mother.

Go against it and try to take Father,
and Father himself would not acknowledge Hikaru.

So from the bottom of this dark, Hikaru cannot move.

As the one robbed, I began.
If the road to taking back is closed, then at that beginning I must remain, forever. No other way of being is there.

...That is why Hikaru is here.
Always here.

<ruby>原点<rt>はじまり</rt></ruby>の記憶。

　父を奪う母。
　母に奪われる父。
　父を失う己。

　繰り返し。
　また、繰り返し。

　おれは同じ夢を見続ける。
　果てもない暗黒の界で。

　それだけが光という存在に許されたこと。

　闇は決しておれを逃さない。
　ここで朽ちよと、そう命ずる。

　動いてはならぬと、そう命ずる。

　そう。
　光は、ここから動いてはならぬ。

　父を奪われた<ruby>光<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>がこの生命を動かすならば、
　それは父を取り戻すためである。

　奪われたおれは、
　奪い返すためだけに<ruby>生きる<rt>うごく</rt></ruby>。

　だがそれは許されぬのだ。

　――父は母のもの。母は父のもの。
　子が母から父を奪うは、<ruby>倫理<rt>ひとのみち</rt></ruby>が厳に禁ずるところ。

　光は、人である。
　人の道に背くことはできぬ。

　人の道に従うならば、
　母から父を取り戻すことは許されぬ。

　人の道に背いて父を奪わんとしても、
　父は光を認めまい。

　だから、光はこの闇の底から動けない。

　奪われた者として始まったおれは、
　奪い返す道が開かれぬ以上、未来永劫<ruby>原点<rt>はじまり</rt></ruby>に留まり
続けるしか<ruby>在様<rt>ありよう</rt></ruby>が無い。

　……だから光はここにいる。
　いつまでもここにいる。
